To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the pharmacokinetics of a coitally-independent, long-acting, multipurpose prevention technology (MPT) were evaluated in macaques over 35 days using an innovative MPT pod-intravascular ring (IVR).
a coitally-independent, long-acting MPT pod- IVR could potentially prevent HIV, HSV, pregnancy, and sexually transmitted infections (STIs).

a coitally-independent multipurpose prevention technology pod-intravascular ring delivering the antireviral agent tenofovir, the antiviral agent acyclovir, and a combination of the hormonal contraceptives etonogestrol and ethinyl estradol was evaluated for pharmacokinetic release in a macaque animal model.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and evaluation of novel multipurpose prevention technologies for women’s reproductive and HIV prevention needs.
the development of novel, multipurpose, coitally independent prevention technology (MPT) for HIV, HSV and unintended pregnancy.

the development and evaluation of a multipurpose pod-intra-vaginal ring that delivers antiretrovirals (ARVs) for the prevention of sexually transmitted HIV, anti-Herpes simplex virus type 2 (HSV-2) drugs, and hormonal contraceptives to prevent unintended pregnancy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the MPT-pod-IVR could serve as a powerful biomedical tool to prevent women’s sexual and HIV infections and unintended pregnancy, which could be an effective tool for women’s sexual and reproduction health.
the pharmacokinetic profile of the MPT-pod-IVR in this study was promising and may be sufficient to provide protection against HIV, HSV, as well as unintended pregnancies.
a coitally-independent MPT-pod-IVR may provide a potent biomedical prevention option for women’s sexual and reproductive health.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed and tested a multipurpose prevention technology (MPT) that can prevent HIV and HSV and unintended pregnancy.
the pharmacokinetic profiles of the MPT-pod-IVRs in macaques are promising for future development of an MPT that could protect women from HIV and HSV infection and unintended pregnancy.

we have shown that we can combine three different drugs in a single ring and have the pharmacokinetic profiles of all three drugs be in the range that is expected to provide protection against HIV, HSV, or unintended pregnancy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the pod-IVR platform has the potential to deliver multiple drugs at pharmacologically active levels over long durations of time.
the pharmacokinetics of the three drugs (TAF, EE and ENG) in the MPT IVR are in line with what we would expect for the prevention of HSV, HIV and pregnancy, respectively.
the pod-IVR platform is a viable approach for developing MPTs that can protect women from HIV, HSV, STIs, and unintended pregnancy.
